title: San Francisco → Tokyo — late November 2026
example_notice: Baked-in EXAMPLE report with fictional data (a made-up SFO→Tokyo search) shipped so the site always has something to show, and so future-Sunny has a complete worked reference for the ranked-field format. Not a real Devon trip; prices/award space invented for illustration.

search_params.value: Up to 2 stops per leg (Devon opted to allow up to 2 for this long-haul — that's what opens the award + one-stop field below; nonstop-only would have removed several cheaper rows)

search_params.label: Ranked field
search_params.value: Business cabin (the 2 premium seats) — that's the cabin with real variance worth ranking. Economy is a near-commodity here (~$690 nonstop, low spread) and is summarized in the source table, not ranked row-by-row.

recommendation:
Top of the ranked field is the ANA "The Room" business award via Aeroplan — 88,000 miles + $240 taxes per seat, which converts to about $1,472 of value at a conservative 1.4¢/point. It's a nonstop lie-flat suite for roughly a third of the cheapest cash business fare. Grab it fast if the award space is live — award seats vanish.

That single row IS the recommendation: it's rank 1 because it's the cheapest adjusted price that clears every hard constraint. Everything below it in the table is a real, bookable alternative — so if points-hassle, loyalty, or seat quality matter more to you than the last few hundred dollars, pick a different row on purpose (see the "consider instead" callouts).
recommendation_reasoning:
The award layer crushes cash on this route this window, which is the whole reason Seats.aero is in the process — two nonstop lie-flat J seats at ~1.4¢/point of value is the textbook premium-cabin points-crush-cash case, and it fits a transferable-points household.

The catch is the usual one: award space is volatile and must be grabbed fast, so treat rank 1 as a "decide now" option rather than something to sit on. If it's gone by the time you look, rank 2 (United nonstop award, your own MileagePlus account) is the clean fallback.

Straight cash business only starts around $3,780–$3,950 (JAL / United nonstop), so the cash floor is real money. Open-jaw (NRT-in / HND-out) came in ~$80 over the round-trip baseline — no gateway benefit here. The LAX positioning play pencils out ~$200 cheaper than straight cash, well under the $1,000 business-class threshold, so it stays in the table as a row but is NOT recommended.

ranking.points_valuation_note: Award rows are converted to a cash-equivalent "adjusted price" at a conservative 1.4¢ per point (a business-class rule-of-thumb redemption value, per The Points Guy's monthly valuations — thepointsguy.com/guide/monthly-valuations/). This is a rule of thumb, not a market price: it lets points and cash rows sit on one sortable table. The exact conversion used is shown on every award row below — never hidden as an internal-only calculation. Change the assumption and the ranking can shift.
hard_constraints: Business cabin for the 2 premium travelers (hard requirement) — economy-only itineraries with no J availability were filtered out.
Max 2 stops per leg (Devon's stated tolerance for this trip) — a 3-stop low-cost self-transfer routing was filtered out.
Arrive Tokyo no later than the evening of the intended first full day — one routing that landed after that cutoff was filtered out.
ranking.filtered_out_note: 7 itineraries were evaluated and filtered out BEFORE ranking for violating a hard constraint (wrong cabin / >2 stops / missed the arrival cutoff). They are not shown at all — the table below is real contenders only, not a greyed-out graveyard.

consider_instead.title: United nonstop award — your own MileagePlus account
consider_instead.body: Only ~$38 of adjusted value above rank 1, still nonstop and lie-flat, and it redeems straight from your own United MileagePlus account — no transfer partner, no chasing Aeroplan space, and it earns/credits against status you already hold. If the ~$38 gap is noise to you, this is arguably the better real-world pick: the loyalty value and the "book it in one account" simplicity are worth more than the rounding error.

consider_instead.title: United nonstop CASH ($3,950) — if you'd rather not burn miles
consider_instead.body: If you don't want to spend points at all, the best straight-cash nonstop is United at $3,950 — again your own airline and status, no award-seat volatility to race against, and Polaris is a genuine lie-flat product. It's ~$2,500 more than the award, so this is a "cash is simpler and I value that" call, not a price call.

consider_instead.title: Qatar Qsuite ($4,600, 2 stops) — if the seat is the point
consider_instead.body: The concrete, nameable edge here is the cabin: Qatar's Qsuite is widely rated the best business-class seat flying (fully-enclosed door, quad "double bed" center pairs). If seat quality is what you're actually optimizing, this row wins on that axis alone — at the cost of being the priciest and a 2-stop, much longer travel day. Named explicitly so it isn't smoothed away just because it's not the cheapest.

ranked_note: Ranked ascending by adjusted price — cheapest first. Award rows show the exact points→cash conversion used (1.4¢/point; see the ranking note). market_arbitrage.summary: Tried the US (departure) and JP (destination) markets. Difference was marginal — under 1% on both cabins — so no market arbitrage win on this route this window. Did NOT try a 3rd market (would ask Devon first).

date_matrix.summary: Swept departures Nov 20–23 against returns Nov 30–Dec 3 (economy fare used as the mover). Cheapest pair was depart Sat Nov 21 / return Tue Dec 1 — ~$120/economy seat cheaper than the mid-week-out / weekend-back pair. The ranked field above is priced on this best pair.
date_matrix.best_pair: Depart Sat Nov 21 → Return Tue Dec 1 2026

open_jaw.summary: Tokyo has two viable gateways (NRT and HND), so open-jaw was worth checking. Fly into NRT, out of HND came in within ~$80/seat of the plain round-trip into NRT — essentially flat (it's ranked row 12). No reason to add complexity; the straight round-trip wins.
open_jaw.roundtrip_baseline: Round-trip SFO⇄NRT — business $4,180 per seat cash (ranked row 10 baseline).
open_jaw.openjaw_option: Open-jaw SFO→NRT, HND→SFO — business ~$4,260 per seat (ranked row 12). ~$80 higher; not worth it here.

hub_hacking.summary: Modeled a positioning play: cheap SFO→LAX leg, then a discounted ex-LAX ANA business fare to NRT (ranked row 7). It penciled out to roughly $200/business-seat cheaper than booking straight from SFO.
hub_hacking.threshold_note: Below Devon's $1,000-business-class positioning-flight threshold ($200 < $1,000), so NOT recommended. It stays in the ranked field (row 7) so you can see it, tagged with the separate-ticket caveat — but the saving doesn't justify the risk.
risk_caveats: Separate tickets = NO through-checked bags; reclaim and recheck at LAX.
NO airline rebooking protection across separate tickets — if the SFO→LAX leg is delayed and the LAX→NRT departure is missed, that long-haul seat may have to be re-bought outright.

Buffer-time rule: a same-day positioning leg needs 4–6+ hours of slack minimum; for a high-value business itinerary, arriving LAX the day before is the safer call — especially on a low-cost-carrier positioning leg.

hidden_city_note: Not applicable / not recommended for this trip — it's a round-trip, and hidden-city/throwaway ticketing only ever works one-way or as a final segment, voids the remainder of the ticket the moment a segment is skipped, carries frequent-flyer account-ban risk, and can't through-check bags. Flagged here only so the omission is explicit.
footer_note: Cash prices are point-in-time and expire fast; award space is volatile. Adjusted prices for award rows use a 1.4¢/point rule of thumb (shown per row) — not a market price. Re-verify everything before booking.
